name: Netherlands: Part II package and CTIS upload check
applies_to: the Netherlands package as a whole (plan-level checklist step)

items.check: Form section: cover letter (proposed MREC stated), Dutch invoice-details document under Proof of payment of fee, and the EU GDPR compliance statement.
K1 recruitment and informed-consent procedure on the EU v2.0 template, with a section for every population pathway in the plan.
K2 recruitment material for every trial-specific item addressed to potential participants.
Dutch L1 main information and consent, and one L1 set per population in population_sets whose trigger is true.
L2 other material integral to consent.
Every Dutch site has a CV, a declaration of interest and a signed VGO.
O1 WMO participant-insurance certificate (or a reasoned exemption request) and liability cover evidenced (O2 where not evidenced elsewhere).
P1 on the national Dutch template.
Both the application-level GDPR statement and the Dutch Part II R1 form are complete.
S1 biological-samples form.
Current mandatory national templates used rather than sponsor substitutes.
The protocol describes every consent pathway used in the trial.
Only the Dutch participant information, consent and recruitment materials are submitted for Dutch ethical assessment.
Translation and certification plan for planned non-Dutch-speaking participants (certificate with the first Part II substantial modification).
Administrative documents in the language set in requirements.json.

Blank consent documents at application; no participant-signed forms uploaded; VGO front sheet signed by the institution's board or management; CV preferably unsigned; DoI and GDPR statement without handwritten signature.
Insurance, P1 form, IVO and protocol state the same compensation and coverage arrangements.
EU Clinical Trial number, document version and date consistent across documents.
Sample types, storage, transfers and retention identical in S1, the protocol and the participant documents.
Data flows, controllers, recipients, transfers and retention identical in R1, the GDPR statement, the participant documents and the protocol.
Consent pathways in K1 match the L1 sets in the package and the protocol.
Version dates match the cover letter and the document list.

Documents adapted from the reference package contain all Dutch national additions (IVO structure, insurance appendix, resistance statement, contacts, population documents) and no leftovers from the reference country.
items.applies_when: the Netherlands is not the reference package

items.check: Correct B-S section prefix and CTIS placeholder for each Part II document; Form-section documents in the Form section or Proof of payment of fee.

Unique, self-explanatory title of at most 100 characters: <section code>_<document type>_<subtype>_<country>_<language>_<special attribute>, with only the fields that distinguish the document; participant documents identify the population and Dutch language.
Version and date entered in CTIS metadata, not in the title.
Personal names only where disclosure permits (principal investigator in M1/M2).
Clean, tracked-change, redacted or public and split-file variants clearly distinguished; superseded drafts removed.
Uploaded filename base contains none of ( ) / , . ; | [ ] (the period before the extension is fine).
Uploaded documents are searchable where possible.
Article 11 workaround: every mandatory Part II placeholder holds the official placeholder PDF titled Part_II_placeholder_document_Article_11_workaround.
items.applies_when: the Netherlands receives Part I only under Article 11

items.check: For each document, publication status checked against the current Annex I publication tables (revised CTIS transparency rules; ACT EU guidance v2.2, 30 April 2026).
Publishable documents: personal data and CCI identified separately; public version redacts only qualifying material; signatures never disclosed (CCMO treats signatures as personal data).
No personal data or CCI in public structured fields.
No drafting instruction remains in any document (see content/conventions/template-instructions.md).
Every document approved by the owner in TrialAgents, or the user has explicitly chosen to export unapproved versions.
